sentences.text: CRIMINAL CASE No. 19421 of 2023

BETWEEN:-
 BRIJESH SINGH THAKUR S/O SHRI LAXMAN SINGH,
 AGED ABOUT 49 YEARS, OCCUPATION: BUSINESS  HOUSE NO. 1860/1 NEW SHOBHAPUR POLICE STATION  RANJHI (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI MANISH DATT, SR. COUNSEL WITH SHRI NEERAJ SHAH,
 ADVOCATE)

AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION BARGI DISTRICT JABALPUR (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 (BY MS. SHWETA YADAV, GOVT. ADVOCATE)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER 1.

This is first bail application filed under Section 439 CrPC on behalf of applicant who is in custody since 8.4.2023 in connection with Crime No.160/2023 registered at Police Station Bargi, District Jabalpur (M.P.), for the offence punishable under sections 376 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. Learned Senior counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
Prosecutrix is aged about 33 years.
Incident is said to have taken place on 31.3.2023 but immediately thereafter no report was lodged.
There was delay in lodging of FIR.
Report was lodged on 7.4.2023.
It is further submitted that there is contradiction in FIR, in statement recorded under sections 161 and 164 CrPC.

In these circumstances, applicant may be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: 3. Learned Govt. Advocate appearing for the respondent/State opposed t h e prayer for grant of bail.
It is submitted that applicant had taken the prosecutrix at a secluded place on promise of giving her a job.
Thereafter at this place he has committed rape on her.
In these circumstances, bail application be dismissed.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
5.
Investigation is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
Prosecutrix has improved her version and has explained delay in later statement which has been recorded.

In FIR she submits that she has reported the incident to her mother but said fact has not come to light in her statement recorded under section 161 CrPC and it has also not been stated that her daughter was ill, therefore, there was delay in lodging of FIR.
6. Considering the aforesaid circumstances, bail application filed by the applicant is allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for his appearance before the trial court on the dates to be fixed by the trial court.

8. The applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
C.C as per rules.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE mms Brijesh Singh Thakur vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8650499/
